openings.claim: Refine parent B into a movement-current paper exception slip: the evening clerk updates an existing exception entry whenever its book moves, retaining the previous entry until the new location is checked. This proposes a bounded probe of location accuracy; the full pickup outcome remains unproven.
openings.delta: Replace once-before-opening exception recording with updates tied to actual movement. Keep the slip behind the desk and retain the existing shelves, cart and clerk. Do not change surname storage or add another retrieval mechanism.
openings.prediction: For holds with temporary locations recorded on the slip, fewer stale entries should produce fewer unnecessary second-location searches. O3 stipulates drift, not an observed benefit of updating. Neither this effect nor O4's small cart sample establishes 95% within two minutes or zero wrong-reader handoffs.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative explanation is household-surname misfiling, stipulated in O2: second-location searches and delays persist despite accurate exception entries because the affected books are outside their expected surname region. O5's concentrated arrivals could also leave the overall timing target unmet.
openings.defeat: An evening with verified current exception entries but unchanged exception-related second searches would defeat the proposed causal benefit. Slip upkeep exceeding the ten-clerk-minute daily preparation budget defeats its constrained feasibility; any wrong-reader handoff or fewer than 95% within two minutes defeats full-case success.
openings.probe: Propose one evening using existing paper, pencils and timing sheet. The clerk records entry updates, actual locations, second searches, complete pickup duration and handoff errors, with names kept behind the desk. Count all slip preparation and maintenance toward ten clerk-minutes, including after-opening corrections. Stop the trial if that budget is exhausted. Examine exception-related timing separately while scoring every available-hold pickup against the full requirements.
assumptions: Fit evaluates the bounded, budget-stopped probe; eventual intervention effectiveness is unproven.
The clerk can complete updates and timing records within the preparation and pickup limits; this capability is unverified.
Exception-location drift contributes causally to delays; household mismatches and arrival concentration may dominate instead.
